items.stem: Why do Python threads generally not speed up a CPU-bound pure-Python computation?

options.text: The Global Interpreter Lock lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time
options.rationale: Correct: the GIL serialises bytecode execution, so CPU-bound threads cannot run in true parallel.
Threads share memory; that is not the limitation here.
Python has a threading module; the GIL is the constraint.

options.text: Creating a thread is slower than the whole computation
options.rationale: Thread creation cost is not the reason; the GIL is.

items.explanation: Correct: the GIL serialises bytecode execution, so CPU-bound threads cannot run in true parallel.

items.stem: Which techniques bound or control concurrency when fetching many URLs with asyncio? (Select TWO)

options.text: Limit in-flight requests with an asyncio.Semaphore
options.rationale: Correct: a semaphore caps how many coroutines run the protected section at once.

options.text: Apply per-request timeouts and cancel stragglers
options.rationale: Correct: timeouts plus cancellation stop slow requests from stalling the batch.

options.text: Replace await with time.sleep to pace requests
options.rationale: time.sleep blocks the event loop and stalls all coroutines.

options.text: Run each fetch in its own process for isolation
options.rationale: Spawning a process per I/O request is wasteful and defeats async's purpose.

items.explanation: Correct: a semaphore caps how many coroutines run the protected section at once.; Correct: timeouts plus cancellation stop slow requests from stalling the batch.

items.stem: What happens if you call an async function like data = fetch(url) without awaiting it?

options.text: It returns a coroutine object that never runs until awaited or scheduled as a task
options.rationale: Correct: calling a coroutine just creates it; it must be awaited or scheduled to execute.

options.text: It runs immediately and blocks until done
options.rationale: Calling does not run the body; awaiting or scheduling does.
It is valid syntax; it simply produces an un-run coroutine.

options.text: It runs in a background thread automatically
options.rationale: No thread is created; nothing executes until the loop drives it.

items.explanation: Correct: calling a coroutine just creates it; it must be awaited or scheduled to execute.
